author: Parsifal-2045
body:
#### PR description:

This PR updates the calorimeter-based muon isolation to make use of local reconstruction in ECAL, HCAL and HGCAL, following the example of the seeded e/gamma paths. Muon isolation now reconstruction only the calorimetric regions around HLT muon candidates:
- ECAL: select the barrel digis in regions of dR 0.45 around `hltPhase2L3MuonCandidates`. Then run the multifit, the rechits, the PF rechits and the PF clustering on these digis
- HGCAL: select the digis in regions of dR 0.5. Then run the uncalibrated rechits, the calibrated rechits and the layer clustering on these digis. With `ticl_barre`l, the merged layer clusters also include the regional EB clusters and the HB clusters, as in the full chain
- HCAL: use the e/gamma HB and HE sequences (no HO, HF, and the rho producer, because the muon isolation doesn't use them)

The regions are larger than the isolation cones (0.3 for ECAL, 0.2 for HGCAL), because a cluster at the cone edge can have hits outside the cone. With `alpaka`, the regional HGCAL EE layer clusters come from the CPU producer, as in the e/gamma L1-seeded chain (we might want to change this for both cases).

While working on these isolation changes, I've also noticed that the new isolation seemed to be slower than the previous one using global calorimeter reconstruction. Investigating a bit, I've found that the region selection module, `HLTCaloObjInRegionsProducer`, was the slowest part of the new chain.  For each input object, the module reads the position from the geometry. For an HGCAL silicon cell, HGCalGeometry::getGeometry calculates the cell position and makes a new cell object for all hundreds of thousands of HGCAL cells. This PR makes the module faster in two ways:
- For the HGCAL object types (digis, uncalibrated rechits and calibrated rechits), the module reads the cell positions from the `TICLGeom` product (`TICLGeomHost`), like the layer clustering
- The ECAL and HCAL types continue to use CaloSubdetectorGeometry
- For all object types, the module calculates eta first, then only calculates phi if a region accepts that eta

#### PR validation:

Code compiles and runs, showing a marginal speed-up. The isolation values for muons, computed in 1000 TTbar 200 PU events, match the ones from the previous approach.
title: Use local calorimeter reconstruction for muon isolation
